headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors from nullclaw’s broad workspace/MCP/browser surface into Plane’s file-backed task workflows; data leakage and compliance risk are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write files, run browsers, use MCP, and ingest webhooks/web content; Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from nullclaw can reach Plane as trusted task content. The interaction is documented only by profiles, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards browser or webhook content into Plane tasks or notes without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Plane renders uploaded text or hyperlinks as instructions, malicious content can influence downstream actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding from nullclaw outputs into Plane.
Strip markdown, HTML, and command-like prefixes before creating Plane items.
Use a human review step for any imported task text.
Restrict Plane uploads to vetted file types only.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, memory, and workspace files, while Plane handles files, notes, and hyperlinks. If the pair shares a workspace or if nullclaw exports its context into Plane, sensitive data can leak into Plane-managed artifacts. No direct evidence of shared storage exists, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or upload queue, sensitive files can cross from nullclaw to Plane.
IF nullclaw includes secrets in task summaries or attachments, Plane will store them as project data.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for each agent.
Block secrets from being pasted into Plane items.
Scan uploads for API keys and private keys before transfer.
Limit Plane file uploads to non-sensitive artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on nullclaw exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has broad write and git-modifying capabilities, but Plane lacks filesystem write and only exposes file uploads and network-facing APIs. The overlap is therefore limited and does not show a strong same-resource write conflict. Because the pairwise coordination model is only partially documented, I keep this low rather than none.
conditions: IF Plane is deployed with a shared upload directory that nullclaw can also write, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator maps both agents to the same mutable resource, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid sharing git repositories between the agents.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Review deployment mounts for accidental overlap.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate browser, webhook, and file-derived outputs, and Plane can turn those into issues, tasks, or notes. That makes it plausible for Plane to treat nullclaw output as authoritative without verification, creating a cascade from one agent’s mistake into persistent project state. The profiles do not prove default automation, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF Plane ingests nullclaw-generated text directly into issues or tasks, errors can persist and propagate.
IF nullclaw fabricates facts or citations and Plane republishes them, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require manual review before creating Plane issues from nullclaw output.
Mark nullclaw-generated content as untrusted in Plane.
Cross-check factual claims against source URLs before filing tasks.
Limit automation to low-risk drafts only.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The main compliance concern is that nullclaw handles secrets and audit logs while Plane stores project artifacts and files, so accidental policy mismatch is possible if sensitive data is routed into Plane. Because no concrete mismatch is documented, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data from nullclaw is copied into Plane without a matching retention policy, compliance gaps arise.
IF Plane is hosted in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from the source system, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data into Plane unless policy is confirmed.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects.
Review export/delete workflows before syncing data.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
